final_message:
I've built the recovery plan workbook and a Word summary for the meeting. **Only Scenario 3 meets every requirement.** It catches up all open POs, gets the April PO in transit by Apr 13 and ships the May PO on May 1, with Grill Guard staying on schedule. I recalculated the workbook formulas and they match a separate model of the schedule. I couldn't open the file in Excel itself to check how it looks.

The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders were empty, so the Open Purchase Orders Listing was the only input. The plans need 9,555 sets built between Jan 22 and Apr 30 (Crew Cab 5,520, Extended Cab 4,035), and 8,080 of those by Apr 12.

| | 1. Current capacity & cells | 2. No Grill Guard in cell | 3. 10-hr day (4 wks), no Grill Guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sets built by Apr 30 | 7,305 | 9,045 | 9,555 (+190 spare) |
| Crew Cab Dec–Feb done | Feb 28 | Feb 22 | Feb 22 |
| Extended Cab Nov–Feb done | Apr 2 | Mar 19 | Mar 13 |
| April PO in transit by Apr 13 | No (1,990 short) | No (655 Extended Cab short; done Apr 19) | Yes (45 sets to spare) |
| Sets still open at Apr 30 | 2,250 | 510 (Extended Cab May) | 0 |
| Grill Guard on schedule | Yes (in the cell) | Yes (other cell from Feb 1) | Yes (other cell from Feb 1) |
| **Caught up, May PO on time?** | **No** (clears about May 30) | **No** (May ships short; balance about May 4) | **Yes** |

- **10-hour window:** I scheduled it for Feb 20 to Mar 19, the day after Louis Riel Day, so all 20 extended days are production days. Starting Feb 5 would lose one of them to the holiday and leave only 10 sets of margin on Apr 13. The 30-day notice has to go out by Fri Jan 19.
- **Main risk:** the Apr 13 margin in Scenario 3 is only 45 sets, about a third of a shift. One Grill Guard day back in the running board cell (if the Feb 1 move slips), a delay to the Feb 5 upgrade, or scrap would push Extended Cab April to Apr 13 or later. May would still be met as long as losses stay under 190 sets.

Assumptions you should confirm (all listed in both files):
- **Grill Guard time:** no rate was given, so I assumed 100 units takes one full 8-hour shift each Friday. If it takes less, Scenario 1 gains some capacity.
- **May build order:** I built Crew Cab May before Extended Cab May; the customer only specified the order through April.
- **Holidays:** Easter Monday is treated as a working day.
- **Deadlines:** each PO must be finished the working day before it ships, so April by Apr 12 and May by Apr 30.
- **Inventory:** no finished running boards on hand.
- **Rates:** the stated daily rates are treated as good output, with no allowance for scrap or breakdowns.
- **Totals:** the listing's TOTAL row for open quantity leaves out May; the plan includes it.

The workbook has a Summary tab, an Inputs tab and one daily plan per scenario, all in the same layout. Change an input and the plans and comparison recalculate; the written summaries and Word document are static text and would need updating separately.

DONE

Files are in `outputs/`:
- Running_Board_Recovery_Plan.xlsx
- Running_Board_Recovery_Plan_Scenario_Summary.docx
